# wolf

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of wolf is to generate simple and flexible logging for **R**.

## Installation

You can install the development version of wolf like so:

``` r
pak::pak("github::jmbarbone/wolf")
```

## Example

You can create a new logging object with a call to `wolf()`.
The `Wolf` class contains methods for including built-in handlers.

Simple insert you logging message into the method.

The `"stdout"` handler ensures that all log messages are printed to the console.


```{r}
#| label: setup
library(wolf)
w <- wolf("readme")
w$add_handler("stdout")
w$info("Hello, wolf!")
w$debug("This is a debug message.")
```

The `Wolf` class also has a `$log()` method, which accepts an expression and picks up on conditions that are signaled.

The **message** below is still printed, but we've also stored the message in the signalled condition.

```{r}
#| label: more
hello <- function() {
  message("I'm inside a function")
  NULL
}

w$log(hello())
# NOTE: try() doesn't signal a condition
try(w$log(df$column))
```
